entries.name: Crisp Vector Atlas
entries.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: detailed GeoMarketeer neighborhood illustration style exploration only, not a UI, website or storyboard.
Target dimensions: 1536 x 1024 landscape, same 3:2 aspect ratio as reference image 1, no stretched geometry. One single full neighborhood illustration per output. Pure white background, no mockup card, no typography, no headings, no annotations, no dotted opening-view boundary, no data overlays. Only small metro M transit sign is permitted.

REFERENCE IMAGE 1 = LOCKED COMPOSITION AND CAMERA AUTHORITY. Faithfully retain its full elevated isometric arrangement and density: tall clustered residential apartment towers and shared garden back LEFT, medium-height office cluster upper RIGHT, underground metro entrance with visible stairs middle RIGHT beside the bustling pedestrian plaza, detached low-rise shop and its small parking court center, operating cafe storefront row at BOTTOM foreground, smaller street-edge buildings and roads as drawn. Keep relative positions, heights, street connections, crossings, garden, parked cars, scooters, trees, terrace seating and people. Do not redesign the neighborhood, move buildings, crop the tall towers, simplify to a few isolated houses, or invent a new city. Keep the whole map comfortably visible. Dense but legible with clear separation between architecture, planting and streets.
REFERENCE IMAGE 2 = BLUE PALETTE AND BRAND FEEL ONLY, NOT GEOGRAPHY. White, pale periwinkle and restrained cobalt. Use blue glass and pale blue vegetation throughout; replace reference 1's green and orange/beige with blue family. No green, orange, amber or beige accents. Building lit faces white/ice blue, shadow faces filled pale or medium blue, windows muted deeper blue. Keep saturated cobalt sparse. Visual weight balanced, not oversaturated all-dark-blue buildings.
Narrative continuity: the two-storey BLUE-AWNING storefront WITHIN the bottom foreground cafe row is Sid's proposed unit. Keep its interior vacant/unfitted and its immediate frontage free of cafe tables/customers. Neighboring cafes immediately beside it are operating and have outdoor customers. Do NOT identify the detached central shop as Sid's candidate. Do not show a successful new cafe or any move to another site. No need for TO LET text in these full-view style studies.
Quality: intentional architecture, readable fine detail, plausible small cars, carefully proportioned seated/walking figures, rounded tree crowns, bushes, benches, awnings, glazing and metro stairs. Texture must not overwhelm the shapes. Do not add doubled/tripled contour strokes on every edge. Prioritize filled masses over wireframe. This is an image-based visual target for possible later 3D construction, not a claim of an editable 3D model.

DIRECTION NAME: CRISP VECTOR ATLAS.
Render as a sophisticated finished 2D axonometric vector illustration. Solid white and pale-blue filled architecture with deliberate cobalt outlines on key silhouettes only, one clean fine contour per feature. Clear flat light/shadow planes, no pencil sketch marks, no photoreal shading, no gradients or glossy surfaces. Secondary details use lighter thinner blue strokes or simple filled marks instead of dense facade grids. Streets solid very pale blue with white paint; crowns are rounded scalloped filled blue masses, not spherical glossy 3D or intricate leaf textures. Little people and cars are crisp filled vector shapes with restrained silhouettes. Strong graphic hierarchy makes whole neighborhood legible when small, while measured facade and cafe details reward closer viewing. Fine confident outlines, filled blue shadows, avoid wireframe or technical blueprint appearance. Preserve the exact dense map composition and camera of image 1.

DIRECTION NAME: SOFT MATTE MINIATURE.
Create a premium physically volumetric 3D miniature render of this exact approved neighborhood with NO drawn blue contour lines, NO vector outlines and NO wireframe edges. Architecture is solid smooth white ceramic/plaster with pale-blue shaded sides and carefully beveled corners. Blue glass windows softly reflect the sky, not mirror-like. Soft broad daylight from upper left, very gentle ambient occlusion, delicate contact shadows, matte material finish, naturally readable thickness to roof parapets, balconies, awnings and stairs. Trees are sculpted rounded clustered canopy volumes in pale periwinkle, simplified individual lobes with soft light, restrained bush volume, no foliage particle noise. Cars and people have subtle rounded 3D form, carefully modeled little silhouettes, believable terrace furniture and store interiors. All streets pale blue-gray with white markings; no dark asphalt. Keep facades white and light, use cobalt only sparingly in glazing and awnings. It should feel like a beautifully crafted architectural scale model that could be orbited later, with more depth, material tactility and gentle shadows than a line illustration. No toy-like giant heads, plastic gloss, overgrown trees or photoreal foliage. Full neighborhood in frame, no labels, no UI. Source image 1 controls exact density, layout and camera; source image 2 only controls blue-white palette. The foreground blue-awning candidate must be vacant, no seated patrons immediately in front of it; customers belong to neighboring cafes.

DIRECTION NAME: LAYERED BLUE PAPER CITY.
Render this exact neighborhood as a meticulously crafted paper architectural diorama, distinctly different from both a vector illustration and a smooth ceramic 3D render. ALL visible forms are folded or layered matte white and blue CARDSTOCK: building facades flat folded sheets with crisp creases and finely inset window cutouts; balconies thin stacked card slabs; trees expressive rounded LAYERED PAPER SILHOUETTES with overlapping blue scalloped lobes, not realistic leaves, not textured spherical pom-poms. Bushes are simple nested curled/scalloped card clusters. Awning stripes are clean folded card strips. Cafe tables, little people and cars are dimensional but deliberately paper-crafted shapes with clear silhouettes and restrained details. Sidewalks, crossings and paving use carefully cut flat layers. Use subtle visible paper grain and tiny real thickness along cut edges, soft short cast shadows to reveal layering. Strong material tactility with a sophisticated adult editorial design sensibility, not a children's toy, not rough handdrawing, not corrugated cardboard. White and ice blue primary surfaces, pale periwinkle shadow planes, restrained cobalt glazing and awnings. Keep sky and white paper background white, no beige/brown material, no orange. No ink contour lines at all, define features by paper edges and carefully lit planes. Preserve ALL original districts, buildings, heights, people movement, roads, metro stairs, front cafe row and parking positions from source image 1. Do not flatten buildings into a single sheet or substitute abstract block symbols. This is a detailed architectural paper city, with legible towers at back left and offices at upper right. The foreground blue-awning candidate unit is vacant; operating cafe terraces sit beside it. Full map composition from same elevated isometric camera, no labels, no UI.
